title: Unwritten viva-voce deposit would corrupt — Scripture alone a certain rule
source_text: XXXII. Praeterea solam Scripturam esse certam fidei regulam, traditiones vero quae extra illam proponuntur dubias & incertas esse, inde patet quod si qua pars doctrinae Christianae ab Apostolis solum viva voce tradita, & memoriae hominum commissa, non vero etiam scriptis mandata esset, certe vel illa ad nos non pervenisset, vel saltem non sine multis corruptelis & depravationibus; adeo ut vix purum ab impuro, germanaque ac sincera veritas ab humanis figmentis & commentis addititiis discerni & secerni posset. Tanta est enim hominum perversitas, ignorantia & negligentia, ut quae simpliciter eorum curae & memoriae commissa sunt, oblivioni facile mandentur, & penitus obliterentur, aut saltem variis modis corrumpantur & adulterentur. Ideoque Scripturae usus plane necessarius est ad certam & accuratam rerum memoriam servandam. Quae vero scriptis consignata non sunt, brevi ex hominum memoria delentur, aut fabulis ita implicantur ut verum a falso distingui non possit. Quod multis experienciis manifestum reddi posset. Nam placita Philosophorum, & instituta Rerumpublicarum quae literis tradita non sunt, sed tantum hominum memoriae commissa penitus interierunt, neque de iis quicquam amplius scitur, nisi si quid forte obiter ab aliquo literis mandatum est. Denique de omnibus illis quae praeteritis temporibus sive gesta, sive dicta sunt, nihil certi habemus praeter ea quae libris tanquam fidis custodibus data sunt asservanda. Si autem Scripturae usus ullibi necessarius est, certe praesertim in iis quae ad religionem & cultum divinum pertinent, circa quae homines natura maxime obliviosi sunt, & ad mentiendum & confingendum proni. Atque in hujus rei fidem Pontificios rogare possumus, ubi nunc sint illae Judaeorum traditiones quas volunt illos a Mose & Prophetis accepisse. Certe ne ipsi quidem Pontificii explicare audent, aut possunt quid traditionibus illis continebatur. Neque de Judaeorum religione & cultu quicquam certi hodie habemus aliunde quam ex Mosis & Prophetarum scriptis.
pass_a_gloss: Furthermore, that Scripture alone is a certain rule of faith, but that the traditions which are proposed outside it are doubtful and uncertain, is plain from this: that if any part of Christian doctrine had been handed down by the Apostles only by living voice and committed to men's memory, and had not also been put into writing, certainly either it would not have reached us, or at least not without many corruptions and depravations; so that scarcely could the pure be discerned and separated from the impure, and genuine and sincere truth from human fictions and added inventions. For so great is men's perversity, ignorance, and negligence, that what is simply committed to their care and memory is easily consigned to oblivion and utterly obliterated, or at least corrupted and adulterated in various ways. And therefore the use of Scripture is plainly necessary for keeping a certain and accurate memory of things. But what is not consigned to writings is shortly erased from men's memory, or so entangled with fables that the true cannot be distinguished from the false. Which could be made plain by many experiences. For the opinions of the Philosophers, and the institutes of Commonwealths which were not handed down in letters but only committed to men's memory, have utterly perished, and nothing more is known of them except if by chance something was put into writing in passing by someone. Finally, concerning all those things which in past times were either done or said, we have nothing certain except what was given to books as to faithful custodians to be kept. But if the use of Scripture is anywhere necessary, certainly especially in those things which pertain to religion and divine worship, about which men are by nature most forgetful, and prone to lying and inventing. And for the faith of this matter we can ask the Pontiffs where now are those traditions of the Jews which they claim they received from Moses and the Prophets. Certainly not even the Pontiffs themselves dare or are able to explain what was contained in those traditions. Nor do we have anything certain today about the Jews' religion and worship from elsewhere than from the writings of Moses and the Prophets.
pass_b_english: Scripture alone is a certain rule of faith; traditions proposed outside it are doubtful and uncertain.

If any part of Christian doctrine had been left by the Apostles only viva voce, committed to memory and never written, it either would not have reached us, or would have reached us thick with corruptions — so that pure truth could hardly be separated from human inventions.
Men's perversity, ignorance, and negligence easily bury, erase, or adulterate what is trusted only to care and memory. Writing is needed for a sure and accurate record.
What is not written soon vanishes from memory or is tangled in fables until true and false cannot be told apart.

Philosophers' opinions and commonwealth institutes left only to memory have perished, except scraps someone happened to write. Of past deeds and sayings we have nothing certain except what books kept as faithful custodians.
If writing is needed anywhere, it is needed most in religion and worship — where people are by nature forgetful and quick to invent.

Ask Rome where the Jews' alleged Mosaic and prophetic oral traditions are now: even Rome cannot say what they contained. Of Jewish religion and worship we know nothing certain except from Moses and the Prophets in writing.
